clue.text: Republic has areas in which crime is a problem

indicators.note: says the shuffled word sits within the pair of letters for areas

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two areas give two As

indicators.note: a word that is a problem has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country is said to have districts where lawbreaking is rife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crime' and 'problem' fit the surface as a social issue; here they are anagram fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a federal republic, commonly called by this shorter name.

clue.text: A blend of mostly tropical fruit

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters that follow are mixed into a new order
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A juice blend made largely from exotic produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TROPICAL to TROPICA, and 'A blend of' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Choose wrought iron case, oddly, for delicate circuitry

parts.note: to choose is to elect

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters of iron are reworked
take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word case

explanation.surface: Picking a casing made of worked iron to protect fragile wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought' makes RONI from IRON; 'oddly' takes C and S from CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronics are circuits built from small, fragile components such as transistors and chips.

clue.text: Sing refrain for musical gathering

indicators.note: the letters wanted are gathered up from across the words refrain for musical

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform the chorus at a concert-style get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' looks like the musical instruction that fits the surface, but it is the slang sense: to sing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang to sing is to tell tales to the authorities, to grass or squeal.

clue.text: Joined United in league

explanation.surface: A footballer signed for United, a team in the league.
explanation.definitionFit: Associated means linked together, either simply connected or formally allied as partners.

clue.text: A fellow made a run for it after wife went on too much

indicators.note: the pieces before it come after the letter for wife

parts.note: to make a run for it is to flee, past tense fled

explanation.surface: A man bolted once his wife had been nagging at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To waffle is to talk at length without saying much, a British informal usage.

clue.text: Drop of whiskey and punch

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to punch is to hit

explanation.surface: A small measure of whiskey mixed into a punch bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit, much as a drop is.

clue.text: Following diversion, ultimately become very gloomy

indicators.note: the rest of the pieces follow the word for diversion

parts.note: a diversion is entertainment, fun

indicators.note: take the last letter of become

parts.note: real is used informally for very, as in real good

explanation.surface: After some amusement, things eventually turn dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: Funereal means suited to a funeral, hence dismal and sombre.

clue.text: Toss up ball endlessly

indicators.note: both end letters of the word for ball are removed

parts.note: a globe is a ball

explanation.surface: Throwing a ball high in a game of catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips G and E from GLOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to throw or hit something in a high arc, a toss up in the air.

clue.text: I eat dry crackers, given this advice?

definitions.text: I eat dry crackers, given this advice?

indicators.note: crackers means mad, so the letters of I eat dry go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone on a slimming plan explains why they only munch plain biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits being eaten, but it signals the anagram of I EAT DRY; the whole clue is the kind of guidance a nutritionist gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary advice is guidance about food, such as sticking to dry crackers.

clue.text: Port Vale's opener goes in very scrappily

indicators.note: done scrappily means messily, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the first letter of Vale leaves the word very
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A football report: Port Vale's first goal goes in after a messy scramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port Vale' is a football club, but 'Port' alone is the definition. Taking V from VERY leaves ERY, which 'scrappily' rearranges. RYE is an old harbour town in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye in East Sussex is a historic harbour town, one of the Cinque Ports' associated towns.

clue.text: Popular myth surrounds quiet Scottish island

indicators.note: the word for myth goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a fable is a myth or legend
sh is a call for quiet
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

explanation.surface: A well-loved legend tells of a peaceful island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small island off the west coast of Scotland, famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fashionable is in vogue, widely liked at the moment.

clue.text: Damaged picture frames about to be reduced

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the letter for about, like a frame round a picture
damaged means broken, so the letters of picture are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A damaged painting's frame is marked down for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' turns PICTURE into CUTPRIE, which 'frames' C inside, just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-price goods are sold at a lowered price, so they are marked down.

clue.text: Mistakes are to be reversed, soldiers trapped at the front admitted

indicators.note: the soldiers and the letter are let into the turned-round word
the word are is read from back to front

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

indicators.note: take the front letter of trapped

explanation.surface: Errors are to be undone, with captured troops confessing at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a stock crossword abbreviation for soldiers; 'admitted' places the new letters after the second letter of the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are a list of errors found in a printed book, from the Latin for mistakes.

clue.text: Expressing regret, a game show admits wrongdoing

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: the word for show lets in the word for wrongdoing

parts.note: a gig is a live performance or show
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A game show host is sorry and owns up to cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry is the act of conveying regret for something done.

clue.text: Golf balls new players hit, finally gaining control

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an over in cricket is a set of six balls
men are the players in a team

indicators.note: take the last letter of hit

explanation.surface: A golf game where fresh players strike the balls and end up in command.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an OVER is a set of six balls bowled by one player, so 'balls' gives OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Government is the exercise of authority over a state or body, its rule and direction.

clue.text: Drive to Oslo regularly

indicators.note: take every other letter of Oslo, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A road trip to the Norwegian capital made often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a verb about motoring to Oslo, and it is, but in the dated sense of cruising along: to tool along.
explanation.definitionFit: To tool is an informal verb for driving along in a leisurely way.

clue.text: Half of party goes with rhetoric — room for improvement?

indicators.note: keep only the first half of the word for party

parts.note: Labour is a major UK political party
oratory is the art of rhetoric, public speaking

explanation.surface: Half a political party relies on fine speeches, so there's room to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock phrase: a lab is literally a room where things are developed and improved.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room for experiments, where products and techniques get developed and refined.

clue.text: The star beginning to oscillate could become dimmer, possibly

indicators.note: the letters could become something else once rearranged
take the first letter of oscillate

explanation.surface: A star that starts to flicker might turn fainter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dimmer' looks like a comparison of a fading star, but it is a noun: a light dimmer switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor, the device used in a light dimmer, so dimmer is an example.

clue.text: Need to be composed after female just panicked

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: just means fair or right

indicators.note: to be composed is to be put together, so the letters of need are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who has just lost her nerve is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like calm, the opposite of the definition, but it signals the anagram ENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened means scared, gripped by fear, which is what panic is.

clue.text: Leader of forgotten tribe dances around large tree

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the shuffled letters go around the letter for large
the letters of tribe dance into a new order

explanation.surface: A chief of a lost people dances round a big tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' turns TRIBE into IBERT, which goes 'around' L after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is a hazel, specifically the cultivated hazel that bears nuts.

clue.text: Run over wild animal

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for run is written backwards

parts.note: to run is to flow, as water does

explanation.surface: A motorist hits a creature from the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' looks like a phrase about a road accident, but 'over' alone is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is a wild member of the dog family.

clue.text: Two supporters used to get the Blades going

definitions.meaning: a pair of things that support: a team follower and the strap that holds trousers up

definitions.text: used to get the Blades going
definitions.meaning: the engine part that drives a car's cooling fan, turning its blades

explanation.surface: A pair of fans helped spur on the Blades, Sheffield United's nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blades are Sheffield United football club, but here they are the blades of a car's cooling fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan belt in a car engine drives the cooling fan, setting its blades turning.

clue.text: Revolutionary vehicle keeps empty spacecraft supplied with oxygen

indicators.note: the word for vehicle holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A rocket carrier holds a fuel-less craft topped up with oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sits with spacecraft and vehicles as if about orbiting, but means Fidel Castro, leader of the Cuban revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution of 1959 and ruled Cuba for decades.

clue.text: Capital of Sweden consumed by liberal opinion — outwardly

indicators.note: the letter for Sweden is eaten up inside the word for liberal

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: take only the outside letters of opinion

explanation.surface: Stockholm's progressive views seem liberal on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Sweden' wants to be STOCKHOLM, but 'Capital' alone is the definition and 'Sweden' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal.

clue.text: Home by five when in old reserved occupation

parts.note: in means at home
V is the Roman numeral for five
as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: the word in keeps the letter for old in reserve inside it

explanation.surface: Getting home by five o'clock from an old job kept for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' looks like a job, matching 'reserved occupation', but it is the military sense of taking over a country.
explanation.definitionFit: An invasion is a hostile entry into territory, leading to its military occupation.

clue.text: With its arrival, I dashed for cover

definitions.text: With its arrival, I dashed for cover

indicators.note: the word for dashed covers the letter I

parts.note: to dash is to run, past tense ran

explanation.surface: When the downpour came, I hurried to shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: what came was a shower, so I fled indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden shower of falling water is what sends people running for shelter.

clue.text: Clutching drink, step into hospital department to see one who deals with piles

indicators.note: the combined piece goes into the department's letters

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: the word for step clutches the word for drink

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A patient with a cuppa goes into a hospital ward to be treated for haemorrhoids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles' suggests the medical complaint in a hospital, but means grand houses; ENT is the ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent sells property, and a pile is a large impressive house.

clue.text: Violent criminal shipping heroin in vessel

indicators.note: shipping out means getting rid of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a thug is a violent criminal
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A thug smuggling drugs aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping' looks like smuggling the drug, but here it means sending it away.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful boat used to tow larger ships.

clue.text: A bridge player possesses clubs and diamonds

indicators.note: the pair of letters holds the letter for clubs

parts.note: a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
E is East, one of the four players in bridge
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A card player holds a hand with both clubs and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like a card suit beside clubs, but it is slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter.

clue.text: Heavyweight reportedly gets purse

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word for heavyweight is taken by its sound

parts.note: a titan is a heavyweight, a person of great power

explanation.surface: A champion boxer collects his prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purse' looks like a boxer's prize money, but is the verb, as in pursing the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: To purse the lips is to draw them tight, contracting them.

clue.text: Grand Hotel, given time, embraces good idea

indicators.note: the run of letters holds the letter for good inside it

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, thou for short
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grand hotel, given enough time, welcomes a fine proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: THOU is informal for a thousand, which is also what a grand means. 'embraces' puts G just before HT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought is a notion or idea that comes to mind.
